judgment.notes: The time partial is completely typed on the positive-time domain with componentwise real derivatives and an explicit zero fallback. This is a total convention, not an assumption of differentiability. On smooth input it coincides with the original time derivative. The local zero extensions used for sources are declared in R001 and leave this global domain unchanged.

Defines precisely the time derivative of D001 on the same positive-time domain, componentwise with its total convention. D001 is declared as its sole definition dependency; no scalar multiplier regularity or second-derivative identity is assumed in the definition.

The family of first spatial coordinate partials has explicit index range 1,…,n, spatial/time arguments and vector codomain. The fixed-index abbreviation has one meaning. The same total derivative convention as D001 makes it well-defined without importing smoothness; H001/H002 remain hypotheses rather than properties of this definition.

The repeated j-coordinate derivative of D003 is typed on the same family and domain, with an unambiguous fixed-j abbreviation and total convention. It defines exactly the pure second spatial partial used in the original componentwise Laplacian and assumes no integration-by-parts or regularity fact.

Defines the j-spatial derivative of the already defined time derivative, not an assumed commuting derivative. All arguments and index range are specified. The other mixed-derivative order is explicitly an output of N002, so no mixed-partial theorem is smuggled into notation.

The finite vector sum of the pure second spatial partials is exactly the componentwise spatial Laplacian, with no time component or sign change. The summation binds j over 1,…,n and D004 provides its summands; there is no unproved PDE assertion in this definition.

The scalar energy density is precisely the unhalved squared time derivative plus the finite sum of squared spatial partials. Euclidean squared norm/dot-product and Frobenius interpretation and Lebesgue dx are explicitly identified. This definition does not grant support, measurability or integrability; those are exported by N002.

Defines the scalar partial time derivative of D007 on positive times with explicit total convention. Classical existence and the differentiated-density formula are not assumed here but are part of N002. There is no hidden derivative/integral exchange in the definition.

The energy is the finite Lebesgue integral of D007 on all spatial space at each positive time, exactly as in the original. Its integrability guard N002 is explicit. N002's producer does not use E; R003 and R005, the inferences using D009, both directly list N002. Thus there is no circular finiteness construction, and no definition or continuity at time zero is assumed.
